techniques.name: Random Forest (Ensemble Learning)
advantages: Extreme computational efficiency during line-rate inference
Intrinsic robustness to monotonic transformations and irrelevant features
limitations: Degraded generalization against structurally novel zero-day exploits
Large memory footprint for ultra-deep tree ensembles

techniques.name: Support Vector Machine (Kernelized SVM)
advantages: Rigorous mathematical foundation minimizing structural risk
limitations: Quadratic to cubic training complexity O(N^2 - N^3)
Slow inference per packet due to support vector kernel evaluations
High sensitivity to feature scaling and hyperparameter tuning

techniques.name: Deep Autoencoders (Reconstruction Anomaly Detection)
advantages: Superior zero-day attack identification without requiring attack signatures
Learns complex non-linear latent manifolds of benign network traffic
End-to-end representation learning bypassing manual feature engineering
limitations: Black-box lack of interpretability impeding SOC incident triage
High computational cost requiring GPU acceleration for real-time retraining
Susceptible to threshold tuning drift in dynamic network environments
